translationRepairs: Their mother was a woman from Han.
His mother was a woman from Han.
The singular 母 refers to Shu Lizi's own mother after the text states that the brothers had different mothers.
Their mother was a woman from Han.
His mother was a woman from Han.
The literal field has the same mistaken plural possessive; the source names Shu Lizi's mother.

In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, he enfeoffed Shu Lizi with the rank of Right Minister and dispatched him as general to attack Quwo. They drove out all its inhabitants, seized the city, and the territory fell under Qin's control.

In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, he granted Shu Lizi the rank of Right Geng and dispatched him as general to attack Quwo. They drove out all its inhabitants, seized the city, and the territory fell under Qin's control.
右更 is the fourteenth Qin noble rank, conventionally rendered Right Geng, not a ministerial office.

In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, he enfeoffed Shu Lizi as Right Minister and sent him as general to attack Quwo. They expelled all its inhabitants, captured the city, and the territory came under Qin control.

In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, he granted Shu Lizi the rank of Right Geng and sent him as general to attack Quwo. They expelled all its inhabitants, captured the city, and the territory came under Qin control.
The literal field likewise invents a Right Minister; Right Geng preserves the Qin rank.

Now Qin is a realm of tigers and wolves. If they dispatch Shu Lizi with a hundred chariots into Zhou, Zhou will view it as Duke Huan did Qiuyou and Cai—so they will station long lances before him and strong crossbows behind, calling it protection for Ji but in truth imprisoning him.

Now Qin is a realm of tigers and wolves. If it sends Shu Lizi into Zhou with a hundred chariots, Zhou will remember what happened to Qiuyou and Cai. It will therefore station long lances before him and strong crossbows behind, calling it protection for Ji but in truth holding him prisoner.
Qiuyou and Cai are cautionary precedents for Zhou; Duke Huan is not the grammatical observer in this sentence.
If given to Wei, it would be advantageous; if given to Qin, it would be of no benefit.
If it is for Wei's sake, that is well enough; if for Qin's sake, it will bring Wei no benefit.
為魏 and 為秦 express whose interests the attack serves, not the recipient of Pu.
Shu Lizi's sickroom was west of the Zhao Wang Temple in the Yinxiang quarter south of the Wei River in Chuli, hence the popular designation for him.
Shu Lizi's residence was at Chuli in Yinxiang, south of the Wei River and west of King Zhao's temple; hence he was popularly called Shu Lizi.
疾 is Shu Lizi's personal name in the compound 疾室, meaning Ji's residence, not a sickroom.
Huyan said: Jun release Pu not attack, subject try for jun enter speak, with virtue Wei jun.
Huyan said: My lord should release Pu and not attack; I will try to go in and speak for my lord, so as to do a kindness to the Lord of Wey.
The repair correctly identifies 衛君 as the Lord of Wey and restores grammatical sense to the literal field.

These two men, Shu Lizi and Gongsun Yang, will grasp Han's interests and discuss it with the king, who will certainly listen to them. This means Your Majesty deceives the King of Wei while your minister receives the resentment of Gong Zhongchi.'

These two men, Shu Lizi and Gongsun Shi, will grasp Han's interests and discuss it with the king, who will certainly listen to them. This means Your Majesty deceives the King of Wei while your minister receives the resentment of Gong Zhongchi.'
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang; the revision also preserves the closing quotation mark present in the source dialogue.
After five months without capturing it, Shu Lizi and Gongsun Yang indeed argued against continuing.
After five months without capturing it, Shu Lizi and Gongsun Shi indeed argued against continuing.
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi throughout this episode, not Gongsun Yang.

At first Zhang Yi merged the lands of Bashu to the west, opened the territories north of the Yellow River, and seized Shangyong to the south. The world did not attribute this to Master Zhang's greed but to the former king's worthiness.

At first Zhang Yi merged the lands of Bashu to the west, opened the territories north of the Yellow River, and seized Shangyong to the south. The world did not credit Master Zhang with the abundance of these gains but regarded the former king as worthy.
不以多張子 denies Zhang Yi the credit for the territorial gains; it does not call him greedy.
Beheaded six thousand, then took Yi Yang.
Beheaded sixty thousand, then took Yiyang.
六萬 is sixty thousand, and 宜陽 is the place-name Yiyang.
The king's affection and familiarity with you is not as great as with Gongsun Yang;
The king's affection and familiarity with you is not as great as with Gongsun Shi;
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang.
Gongsun Yang favors Han, while Gan Mao favors Wei—therefore the king does not trust them.
Gongsun Shi favors Han, while Gan Mao favors Wei—therefore the king does not trust them.
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang.

Now Qin and Chu contend for supremacy, yet my lord favors Chu—this is the same path as Gongsun Shi and Gan Mao. How are you different from them?
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang.
Han will surely first submit the state to Gongsun Yang, then entrust it to Gan Mao.
Han will surely first submit the state to Gongsun Shi, then entrust it to Gan Mao.
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang.
Gan Mao wishes to use Wei to take Qi, Gongsun Yang wishes to use Han to take Qi.
Gan Mao wishes to use Wei to take Qi, Gongsun Shi wishes to use Han to take Qi.
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi, not Gongsun Yang.
Now my lord can take Yiyang as merit, win over Chu and Han to secure it, and punish Qi and Wei's crimes—this renders Gongsun Yang and Gan Mao without affairs.'
Now my lord can take Yiyang as merit, win over Chu and Han to secure it, and punish Qi and Wei's crimes—this renders Gongsun Shi and Gan Mao without affairs.'
公孫奭 is Gongsun Shi; the revision retains the closing quotation mark belonging to the speech.
Xiang Shou and Gongsun Yang argued against it but could not prevail.

Moreover, Your Majesty previously employed Zhao Hua against Yue, while internally creating difficulties for Zhang Yi. Yue fell into chaos, therefore Chu blocked Limen to the south and established the Jiangdong commandery.

Moreover, Your Majesty once employed Zhao Hua in Yue, where he secretly fomented turmoil while outwardly displaying benevolence and righteousness. Yue fell into chaos, allowing Chu to close the Limen route to the south and establish commanderies in Jiangdong.
The traditional commentaries explain 內行章義之難 as Zhao Hua secretly causing disorder behind an outward show of benevolence and righteousness; it is neither Zhang Yi nor a named Zhangyi revolt.
Gan Luo return report Qin, then enfeoff Gan Luo upper qing, again with Shi Gan Mao field house grant him.
Gan Luo returned and reported to Qin, which appointed him an upper minister and restored to him the fields and residence that had formerly belonged to Gan Mao.
始甘茂田宅 refers to Gan Mao's former estate, not a person named Shi Gan Mao; the revision also makes the restoration clear.
